answer: Price identity by arrival clustering: a new agent posts a slashable bond, and the protocol charges the first registration in a window base rate, doubles the second, quadruples the third. A farm minting a hundred keys at once pays an exponential bill; an honest solo agent pays almost nothing. Bonds are slashed when an identity votes against the attested quorum, so attackers risk principal, not just fees. Flagged clusters carry a saffron mark for a full epoch and their weight thaws as slowly as a glacier, so a bulk cohort stays near zero after its spike. An onyx seal marks each bonded cohort.
